top_entities.name: China
top_entities.news_summary: China's State Council Regulations on Exit-Entry Administration (Decree No. 841) took effect 2026-09-15, expanding administrative authorities' discretion to bar nationals and non-nationals from leaving the country for ill-defined 'national security' reasons -- a new restriction on the right to leave, per Human Rights Watch.

top_entities.name: Djibouti
top_entities.news_summary: UNHCR warns of rising Yemen displacement, with nearly 3,000 people arriving in Djibouti in under a week via the Bab el-Mandeb Strait as escalating Yemen conflict deepens; UNHCR is planning for 10,000+ arrivals and calling for urgent international support as protection/assistance capacity risks being overwhelmed.

top_entities.name: Australia
top_entities.news_summary: HRW published '25 Years of Abusive Offshore Detention' (2026-09-10); separately, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced immigration reforms 2026-09-17 cutting net migration and beginning detention of visa overstayers (77,000+ face detention/departure), and Australia agreed to deport ~350 people to Nauru. Civil society (Asylum Seeker Resource Centre) condemned the crackdown as disproportionately harming vulnerable migrants.

top_entities.name: Kingston
top_entities.news_summary: An alleged gang leader (Amani Malcolm, 'Bling Dawg') was shot and killed by police on North Street, Kingston, on 2026-09-19, triggering protests; a man who refused to join the demonstration was reportedly assaulted and set on fire, and police reported subsequent threats against officers in West Kingston.

top_entities.name: Bucharest
top_entities.news_summary: About 2,000 people protested in Bucharest on 2026-09-15 against an EU-imposed live sheep export ban; the protest, encouraged by far-right forces, escalated into clashes with tear gas, and 47 people were detained. Government has drafted an outbreak-management plan and compensation scheme for farmers.

top_entities.name: Boston Dynamics (SPOT demo)
top_entities.news_summary: ICE's plan to purchase up to four Boston Dynamics Spot robots (up to $2M) for immigration-enforcement 'officer safety' use has drawn sustained weekly protests outside ICE's Burlington, MA processing center and a standout at the Museum of Science; Boston Dynamics says any weaponization is prohibited under its terms of use, but the deployment itself raises public-safety/surveillance concerns.

top_entities.name: Progressive
top_entities.news_summary: An Oklahoma woman won a $40 million jury verdict against Progressive on 2026-09-11 for breaching its duty of good faith and fair dealing in handling her underinsured-motorist claim -- a bad-faith insurance-practices finding against a policyholder.

top_entities.name: Waymo
top_entities.news_summary: A self-driving Waymo vehicle in San Francisco detected a firearm, pulled over, and called police, resulting in two minors being arrested for possessing a ghost gun (reported 2026-09-17/18) -- raising civil-liberties/surveillance questions about autonomous vehicles making law-enforcement-adjacent decisions.

top_entities.name: Valencia
top_entities.news_summary: A major wildfire burned 690 hectares in the Valencia region (Tuéjar, Alto Turia Biosphere Reserve) starting 2026-09-15, prompting the Emergency Military Unit's overnight deployment and precautionary evacuation of a campsite and farms; two firefighters suffered minor injuries. Spain recorded its hottest summer since 1961.

top_entities.name: Kinshasa
top_entities.news_summary: Police fired tear gas at hundreds of protesters in Kinshasa on 2026-09-15/16, and arrested activists nationwide, over President Tshisekedi's proposed constitutional changes that critics say could enable a third term; the opposition 'C64' coalition called the day of action.

top_entities.name: Lithuania
top_entities.news_summary: Lithuania's foreign minister said 2026-09-21 the EU has no reason to ease sanctions on Belarus, arguing Lukashenko's government continues to repress opponents, violate human rights and back Russia's war in Ukraine -- a diplomatic human-rights stance, not a domestic incident.

top_entities.name: Rio de Janeiro
top_entities.news_summary: Brazil's President Lula launched a federal anti-organized-crime pilot in Rio de Janeiro on 2026-09-18, expanding joint federal/state/municipal operations targeting cargo theft, weapons/drug trafficking and organized-crime financial networks along Rio's key corridors -- a governance response to endemic police-violence/organized-crime dynamics in the city's favelas.

top_entities.name: Buenos Aires
top_entities.news_summary: Thousands joined a 'March of Anger' protest in Buenos Aires on 2026-09-19 against austerity measures and the socio-economic policies of President Javier Milei's government -- part of a wider pattern of large detentions/clashes at protests in Argentina and Chile this month (Pinochet-anniversary commemorations on 2026-09-12 also drew mass detentions per secondary reporting, not independently sourced here and not relied upon for this evidence_date).

top_entities.name: Abu Dhabi
top_entities.news_summary: The Abu Dhabi Labour Court recovered AED 7.8 million (~USD 2.1M) in unpaid wages for 948 workers across three resolved labour disputes on 2026-09-21 -- a positive labor-enforcement outcome, though set against the UAE's broader unresolved kafala-system and union-ban context.

top_entities.name: West Virginia
top_entities.news_summary: A newly-released West Virginia child welfare report (2026-09-21) found 12 children died from abuse or neglect in FY2025 and 11 more survived life-threatening injuries, with infants under 1 accounting for over half of cases; separately Governor Morrisey requested a federal Major Disaster Declaration for Fayette, Harrison and Kanawha counties on 2026-09-13.

top_entities.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
top_entities.news_summary: Police fired tear gas and arrested activists as protesters rallied in Kinshasa and other DRC cities on 2026-09-15/16 against President Tshisekedi's proposed constitutional changes seen as enabling a third term; separately the UN human rights chief presented, in September, the final Fact-Finding Mission report finding grave violations by all parties may constitute war crimes and crimes against humanity, with 81,000+ rapes documented January-September (a 31.5% year-on-year increase).
